Anthony Barr Picks Bears To Win NFC North Over Lions Jeffrey Becker-USA TODAY Sports Dallin Ballard · Gameday Chitown Fri, November 20, 2026 at 12:45 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North race has narrowed down to two teams, and former Vikings linebacker Anthony Barr believes the Chicago Bears are the ones to beat, according to Yahoo Sports . On "The Jim Rome Show," during a Nov. 16 appearance, Barr clarified that the division title depends on a fight between Chicago and Minnesota. He dismissed the Detroit Lions as a long-term threat despite their current standing at the top of the table. Barr pointed to a specific injury that could sink Detroit's season. For the Lions' defense, it was distressing to witness Aidan Hutchinson's awful injury, according to him. That unit is already taking a hit after struggles over the last two or three years. With Hutchinson out, the Lions lack the defensive anchor needed to close out a tight division race. The Defensive Edge Chicago has a clear path to the top spot because of its improved defensive line. The defensive line's addition of Jeffery Simmons has proven huge, Barr pointed out. This move helps the pass rush and could mask issues in the secondary. While some fans worry about the back end of the defense, Simmons brings a physical presence that changes how offenses attack the Bears. The offense under head coach Ben Johnson is also playing better football right now. Throughout the season, the chemistry and camaraderie between Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams have become evident, Barr observed. They have proven they can score points and move the ball effectively. This balance makes them a dangerous opponent for anyone in the conference. Why the Packers Are Out Green Bay is not part of this conversation, according to Barr. Packers defense still leaves much to be desired, he believes, and they lack any running game. Without a ground attack, the offense cannot control the clock or keep the defense fresh. This inconsistency puts them behind both Chicago and Minnesota in the standings. The Vikings remain a strong contender with the number one defense in the league. Kirk Cousins has given them a breath of fresh air after offensive struggles with previous quarterbacks. However, Barr sees the Bears as the team with the most momentum heading into the final stretch of the season. The division outcome will probably hinge on the two remaining games played between the Bears and Lions. The teams face off on Thanksgiving and then again in their Week 17 showdown in Chicago. The division could be at stake in that final matchup on Jan. 10, 2027, serving as the regular season's last game.

Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Kole Noble, Mike Payton, Tyler Forness, Wendell Ferreira · AtoZ Sports Wed, November 18, 2026 at 9:15 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Three teams stand on top of the NFC North with 7-2 records and the fourth isn't far behind at 6-4 after Week 10. But, only one team will take home the NFC North title and our division beat writers gave their prediction on which team will come out on top. The NFC North race is going to be one of the most exciting storylines to watch over the final eight weeks of the 2026 regular season. After Week 10, all four teams have winning records with the Minnesota Vikings, Detroit Lions, and Chicago Bears all 7-2. All four teams are currently in playoff position and all four teams have legit shots of reaching the postseason. However, only one team is going to land one of the Top-4 seeds as a division champion. With eight weeks left to be played, including six divisional matchups, a lot is at stake over this final stretch. With everything we know and have seen so far, our four NFC North beat writers at A to Z Sports came together to predict which team will win the division. Here's the results, and the explanations to back those selections. Tyler Forness: Minnesota Vikings When I take a look at all these teams, they all make sense, but only one team has a chance to really be historic based on what we've seen the first half of the season. That's the Minnesota Vikings. That defense has figured out over the course of the last four years how to fix all of their holes. First, it was being able to defeat in-breakers. Then, against the Lions in those two games in 2024, it was those short little stop routes to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta that hurt the Vikings. You can't attack in short spaces anymore because of how they drop and take that away from you. You have to beat them with explosives. And other than Jordan Love, in one half, nobody has been able to do it. I really think that this Vikings defense is borderline historic . If they get capable enough play from the offense, like they did against Packers – and they did so without three of their top four pass catching weapons – I think it's going to be a cakewalk to the division title. There's still going to have a lot of battles. There's a lot of football left to be played. Potential injuries could happen, but the only unit that has a chance to be really historic is that Vikings defense, and I am going to take that 10 out of 10 times. Mike Payton: Detroit Lions I'm going to say the Detroit Lions. I mean who else am I going to really say? I'm not saying that just because I cover them. I just think ultimately they're they have the best offense in not just the division but the league. They're scary and they're only getting better and their offensive line is great, and Jahmyr Gibbs is having a LaDainian Tomlinson type year. We'll see if the Lions can do it defensively. Obviously, I'm concerned that Aidan Hutchinson's not here anymore, and Jack Campbell is also not here anymore. But you get Kerby Joseph back this weekend. Brian Branch has been back, and it's already made a huge improvement. DJ Reed will be back. He's been one of the best cornerbacks in the league in the last five six weeks. I think this team's able to get pressure. I think they're able to stop the run. I think they're able to do enough . While I think the Vikings are an amazing defense, I don't trust their offense, even with Kirk Cousins. And I don't trust really anything the Packers are doing right now, they're struggling a lot, especially on that offensive line. The Bears are good and I think they're the other team that's going to be in this race with the Lions. Chicago can be a pretty scary team, but defensively, I think they have some some holes that can be attacked. Overall, I got to go with Detroit here. Kole Noble: Minnesota Vikings The Bears started the season 7-2, including two wins over last season's Super Bowl teams, went into the bye week as the number one team in this division. Things changed in a hurry over the week off with the Bears now third in the North and sixth in the NFC. To me, to win the division, the Bears have to be at least 3-1 in these final four division games, which means you have to beat the Lions twice. I just don't think they can do that . The other thing Chicago HAS to do on top of that is win both trap games, one this week against the Saints, and then going down to Miami later in the season. I don't think the Bears are beating the Bills, and Jacksonville is going to be tough home game. I mean, Chicago simply has a brutal schedule, it's the toughest in the NFL. So I think Minnesota, just with the cakewalk schedule they have left this season, while being 7-2 as well right now, has the best chance. Especially now that the Vikings have average at worst quarterback play to back up a championship-caliber defense. The Minnesota Vikings have a 92% chance to make the NFL playoffs and a 6% chance to win Super Bowl LXI, according to the A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Mon, Nov 16). Wendell Ferreira: Minnesota Vikings I think the Lions will have the problem with without Aidan Hutchinson and adapting to life without him on defense. It'll be hard for Detroit's offense to cover that up. I think the Bears and the Vikings are probably the two best teams at this point in the division, considering everything going on right now. But to Kole's point, the Vikings have a much easier schedule. They are also finding their best version of themselves now that they have a competent offense. I do think the Packers are a good team too, and they can make the playoffs. But because they are two games behind and with a 1-3 division record, they can't get back to the NFC North title race. So, while I think all four teams have a chance to make the playoffs, I do think the Minnesota Vikings win the division when it's all said and done. away.headline: Bears Week 12 Tuesday Injury Report: Updated Report and Analysis
away.blurb: DNP = Did Not Participate, FP = Full Participation The secondary is the biggest concern. Gordon missed both Monday and Tuesday with a shoulder injury, and Hicks was added Tuesday with a concussion. A concussion on a short week is a serious problem for Hicks, since he has to clear every step of the league’s protocol before Thursday. That makes him unlikely to play. Gordon’s two straight DNPs aren’t a good sign either. If both are out, Chicago would be thin at defensive back against one of the league’s most explosive passing attacks, and the depth players behind them would need to step up right away. There’s better news elsewhere. Benedet went from DNP on Monday to a full practice on Tuesday, so his quad injury looks manageable and he should be ready to go. Jackson has been a full participant both days with his elbow and appears to be on the report only as a precaution. Johnson’s ankle is the other one to watch: two DNPs put his status in doubt, which could mean a lighter backfield rotation on Thursday. Wednesday’s final report will settle things, but for now the injuries are mostly in the defensive backfield. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing The Detroit Lions entered a short week with fresh injury concerns on defense ahead of their Thanksgiving showdown against the Chicago Bears. An estimated practice report released Monday listed edge rusher D.J. Wonnum as a non-participant with a back injury and safety Chuck Clark as a non-participant with a hamstring issue. The team held only a walkthrough, so the designations are estimates rather than results from a full session. Wonnum, one of the club’s key offseason additions, had not appeared on the injury report earlier in the week. He returned from a concussion that sidelined him for one game and contributed in Sunday’s 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The back issue raises questions about his availability for Thursday’s game at Ford Field. Head coach Dan Campbell was not asked about either player Monday and is expected to address the situation in his Tuesday news conference. Both absences would test a defense that has begun to stabilize after losing linebacker Jack Campbell and edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson to longer-term injuries. Hutchinson remains on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury. Wonnum has recorded seven sacks in nine games this season, placing him one away from a career high. He played 49 defensive snaps (71 percent) against Tampa Bay, finishing with five tackles, a sack, a pass defensed and a forced fumble. Clark has started every game for Detroit this season and played every defensive snap against the Buccaneers, logging eight tackles, a sack and a pass defensed. The veteran was recently named a team captain after the losses of Campbell and Hutchinson. His absence could accelerate the integration of Kerby Joseph, who returned Sunday after a lengthy absence. The Lions used three-safety packages in that game, with Brian Branch shifting into the slot in nickel looks. Cornerbacks Khalil Dorsey (wrist) and D.J. Reed (hip) were listed as full participants, offering some stability in the secondary. Reed had been inactive for multiple recent games. Detroit (8-2) and Chicago (8-2) enter the game tied atop the NFC North. The Lions will have full practices Tuesday and Wednesday before submitting final injury designations. Campbell has emphasized the next-man-up approach throughout a season marked by absences. While both of these teams have a long way to go before locking up the No. 1 seed, a head-to-head win could go a long way in that race. Mahomes and Allen have a ton of history against each other, meeting four times in the playoffs and 10 times overall. They’ve split the 10 matchups 5-5 with Allen taking control in their recent regular-season tilts. away.blurb: The Buffalo Bills have 14 players officially dealing with some sort of injury, but it's seemingly more and more feasible that the entire group is available for Thanksgiving night despite the short week. "I know it's walkthrough today, but everybody will be out there today. We'll kind of just continue to evaluate it through Thursday. Obviously, not practicing today, but everybody seems like they're in as good of a place as we can be right now," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady on Tuesday afternoon in Orchard Park. That news is nothing less than encouraging for the three Week 12 additions to the injury report coming out of the November 22 win over Miami. Right tackle Spencer Brown, right guard O'Cyrus Torrence and outside linebacker Greg Rousseau, all starters, popped up on Monday's injury report. While the Bills did not practice on Monday, all three earned limited designations with practice status estimations required by the NFL. Tuesday marks a positive step forward for starting cornerback Christian Benford, who was forced out during the second half against the New York Jets on November 15. Having injured his groin, Benford did not practice at all leading up to the November 22 home game. The Bills ruled him out on Friday . Returning to play a full game against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18, Brown did not respond well during the Week 7 bye. He sat out the November 1 win over the Baltimore Ravens. With the back seemingly an issue that Brown will have to manage moving forward, his presence on the injury report is likely due to the fact he's seeking treatment. Brown addressed reporters from the podium on Tuesday, and he did not give any reason to think he would not be available this week. Torrence popped up with an ankle injury one day after playing 99 percent of offensive snaps in Week 11. The rock-solid hog molly will be available to face the Chiefs if history is any indication. away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their second injury report ahead of Week 12's game against the Buffalo Bills. Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker participated in practice for the first time since suffering his groin injury. Andy Reid was asked whether he would play in Week 12, and didn't sound particularly confident. “We'll see,” Reid said. “Let's see how he does today. I just want to get him out there and see. You know, really, he wants to get out there. So, but we'll see how he moves around. He's feeling pretty good, though.” KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related The Chiefs placed FB Ben VanSumeren on injured reserve , so he won't appear on the injury report for the remainder of the week. He must miss at least four games while on IR. Coach Reid described his injury as a knee sprain, so he could realistically return this season. Chiefs RG Trey Smith fully participated in practice. Coach Reid suggested that he's on track to return for Week 12. Chiefs DT Omarr Norman-Lott remains limited in practice as he recovers from his ACL injury.
